title: Sudoku beyond the beginner
description: Generate a 9 x 9 Sudoku with k clues and exactly one solution that a beginner cannot finish: naked and hidden singles, naked and hidden pairs and locked candidates (pointing, claiming) leave at least one cell empty. The beginner's part is in the abstraction: solver A guesses the beginner's pencil marks and requires them to be closed under these techniques while a cell stays empty, which is possible exactly when the beginner gets stuck. Uniqueness is left to the check, as in sudoku-unique. Delete a technique from the beginner fragment to allow it.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The size of the puzzle and the derived domains. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% A 9 x 9 Sudoku: every row, every column and each of the nine 3 x 3 boxes contains the
% values 1..9 once. An instance may print clues pre(R,C,V) and may fix the solved grid with
% solution(R,C,V) (Instances tab).
row(1..9). col(1..9). val(1..9).
box(R,C,(R-1)/3*3+(C-1)/3) :- row(R), col(C).
printed(R,C) :- pre(R,C,_).

fragments.name: sudoku
fragments.description: The rules of the puzzle for any grid; used by solver A (one grid) and solver C (two grids).
fragments.text:
% The rules of the puzzle, for every grid G that a solver declares with grid(G):
% cell(G,R,C,V) says that grid G has the value V in row R, column C.
1 { cell(G,R,C,V) : val(V) } 1 :- grid(G), row(R), col(C).
:- cell(G,R,C1,V), cell(G,R,C2,V), C1 < C2.
:- cell(G,R1,C,V), cell(G,R2,C,V), R1 < R2.
:- cell(G,R1,C1,V), cell(G,R2,C2,V), box(R1,C1,B), box(R2,C2,B), (R1,C1) < (R2,C2).
% Every grid respects the printed clues.
:- grid(G), pre(R,C,V), not cell(G,R,C,V).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): a solved grid and k of its cells as clues.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: a solved grid s and k of its cells that are revealed as clues.
% The grid is the instance's solution/3 if it gives one (then the grounder fixes it, which
% makes every solve call cheaper), otherwise any grid.
fixed :- solution(_,_,_).
grid(s) :- not fixed.
cell(s,R,C,V) :- solution(R,C,V).
:- fixed, pre(R,C,V), not solution(R,C,V).
k { clue(R,C) : row(R), col(C), not printed(R,C) } k.
% given(R,C,V): the puzzle shows the value V in row R, column C.
given(R,C,V) :- clue(R,C), cell(s,R,C,V).
#show given/3.

fragments.name: beginner
fragments.description: Also in solver A: the candidate must leave a beginner stuck (singles, pairs, locked candidates).
fragments.text:
% The beginner works with pencil marks: out(R,C,V) says that V is crossed out in cell
% (R,C), known(R,C,V) that V is written there. The beginner's notes at the end are the
% smallest set that is closed under the techniques below. The puzzle is too hard for the
% beginner if and only if SOME closed set of notes leaves a cell empty (the smallest one
% then does too). So the abstraction guesses the notes and only requires them to be
% closed: every technique becomes a constraint "if the premise holds, so does the result".
{ out(R,C,V) } :- row(R), col(C), val(V).
{ known(R,C,V) } :- cell(s,R,C,V).
stuck :- cell(s,R,C,V), not known(R,C,V).
:- not stuck.

% The units: nine rows, nine columns and nine boxes.
unit(r(R),R,C) :- row(R), col(C).
unit(c(C),R,C) :- row(R), col(C).
unit(b(B),R,C) :- box(R,C,B).
other(U,R,C,R2,C2) :- unit(U,R,C), unit(U,R2,C2), (R,C) != (R2,C2).
peer(R,C,R2,C2) :- other(_,R,C,R2,C2).

% Clues are written; a written value crosses out the other values in its cell and the
% value in the other cells of its units.
:- given(R,C,V), not known(R,C,V).
:- pre(R,C,V), not known(R,C,V).
:- known(R,C,V), val(W), W != V, not out(R,C,W).
:- known(R,C,V), peer(R,C,R2,C2), not out(R2,C2,V).

% The techniques are sound, so a value they write is the value of the candidate's grid s.
% Using s keeps the grounding small.

% Naked single: every other value is crossed out in the cell.
:- cell(s,R,C,V), out(R,C,W) : val(W), W != V; not known(R,C,V).

% Hidden single: V is crossed out in every other cell of a unit.
:- cell(s,R,C,V), unit(U,R,C), out(R2,C2,V) : other(U,R,C,R2,C2); not known(R,C,V).

% Naked pair: two cells of a unit have only V1 and V2 left; cross them out in the rest.
only2(R,C,V1,V2) :- row(R), col(C), val(V1), val(V2), V1 < V2,
    out(R,C,W) : val(W), W != V1, W != V2.
:- unit(U,R,C), val(V1), val(V2), V1 < V2, V = (V1;V2), not out(R,C,V),
    2 #count { R2,C2 : other(U,R,C,R2,C2), only2(R2,C2,V1,V2) }.

% Hidden pair: two values are crossed out in every cell of a unit but the same two cells;
% cross out every other value in those cells. The two values are then the grid's values
% in the two cells, so it suffices to look at those.
except2(U,V,R1,C1,R2,C2) :- other(U,R1,C1,R2,C2), (R1,C1) < (R2,C2), val(V),
    out(R,C,V) : unit(U,R,C), (R,C) != (R1,C1), (R,C) != (R2,C2).
first2(U,R1,C1,R2,C2) :- except2(U,V,R1,C1,R2,C2), cell(s,R1,C1,V).
second2(U,R1,C1,R2,C2) :- except2(U,V,R1,C1,R2,C2), cell(s,R2,C2,V).
hidden2(R1,C1,R2,C2) :- first2(U,R1,C1,R2,C2), second2(U,R1,C1,R2,C2).
:- hidden2(R1,C1,R2,C2), val(W), not cell(s,R1,C1,W), not cell(s,R2,C2,W), not out(R1,C1,W).
:- hidden2(R1,C1,R2,C2), val(W), not cell(s,R1,C1,W), not cell(s,R2,C2,W), not out(R2,C2,W).

% Locked candidates. Pointing: within a box, V is crossed out outside one row (column);
% cross V out in the rest of that row (column).
:- cell(s,R,C,V), box(R,C,B), col(C2), not box(R,C2,B), not out(R,C2,V),
    out(R3,C3,V) : box(R3,C3,B), R3 != R.
:- cell(s,R,C,V), box(R,C,B), row(R2), not box(R2,C,B), not out(R2,C,V),
    out(R3,C3,V) : box(R3,C3,B), C3 != C.
% Claiming: within a row (column), V is crossed out outside one box; cross V out in the
% rest of that box.
:- cell(s,R,C,V), box(R,C,B), box(R2,C2,B), R2 != R, not out(R2,C2,V),
    out(R,C3,V) : col(C3), not box(R,C3,B).
:- cell(s,R,C,V), box(R,C,B), box(R2,C2,B), C2 != C, not out(R2,C2,V),
    out(R3,C,V) : row(R3), not box(R3,C,B).

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the clues with their values. The solved grid stays private to solver A.
fragments.text: glue(given(R,C,V)) :- row(R), col(C), val(V), not printed(R,C).

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for two different grids that agree with all clues (solver C).
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: two different grids a and b that both agree with the clues.
% (One of them may be the candidate's own grid.)
grid(a). grid(b).
:- given(R,C,V), not cell(a,R,C,V).
:- given(R,C,V), not cell(b,R,C,V).
differ :- cell(a,R,C,V), not cell(b,R,C,V).
:- not differ.
#show.
#show a(R,C,V) : cell(a,R,C,V).
#show b(R,C,V) : cell(b,R,C,V).

% Both grids fit every puzzle that shows only values on which they agree. So a clue
% has to appear that contradicts one of them: any value in a cell where a or b has
% another value.
both(R,C,V) :- cell(a,R,C,V), cell(b,R,C,V).
relevant(given(R,C,V)) :- row(R), col(C), val(V), not printed(R,C), not both(R,C,V).

fragments.name: view
fragments.description: A domain view (Observatory tab): the scene part draws what stays, the frame part one step, as draw/1 marks.
fragments.text:
% The grid, boxes in alternating borders; printed clues shaded.
#program scene.
draw(layout(grid)).
draw(cell(R,C)) :- row(R), col(C).
draw(attr(cell(R,C), stroke, box)) :- box(R,C,B), B \ 2 == 0.
draw(attr(cell(R,C), label, V)) :- pre(R,C,V).
draw(attr(cell(R,C), fill, printed)) :- pre(R,C,_).

#program frame.
% The candidate's clues.
draw(attr(cell(R,C), label, V)) :- cand(given(R,C,V)).
draw(attr(cell(R,C), fill, clue)) :- cand(given(R,C,_)).
% A counterexample: two solutions a and b; the cells where they differ show (a, b).
differs(R,C,(V,W)) :- cex(a(R,C,V)), cex(b(R,C,W)), V != W.
draw(attr(cell(R,C), fill, differ)) :- differs(R,C,_).
draw(attr(cell(R,C), label, L)) :- differs(R,C,L).
draw(note("Two solutions fit the clues; they differ in the coloured cells (a, b).")) :- kind(reject).
draw(note("One solution: the puzzle is done.")) :- kind(solution).
#show draw/1.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + sudoku + abstraction + beginner      options "--project"
solver C = shared + sudoku + check      options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)
